Effective communication is a cornerstone of every project. Communications management addresses a wide range of the information needs of the stakeholders, participants, or others involved in the project. Good two-way communications among all stakeholders is key for the success of the project. Good communication forestalls surprises, prevents duplication of effort, and can help to reveal omissions and misallocation of resources early enough to permit corrections. From a project management perspective, some of the most critical communications relate to how information about the project is exchanged between the direct participants. Therefore, one of the first considerations of each project is its organizational structure or governance structure. The governance structure establishes reporting relationships and defines the way project participants interact when they receive information such as status reports or make decisions regarding issues, risks, or scope changes.

Defining the governance structure early in the project addresses matters such as:

  • Who has the authority to approve changes in scope (inclusive of time or cost)?
  • Who is responsible for issue and risk management?
  • How will risks and issues escalate if they remain unresolved?
  • How often are status reports or meetings required?
  • What are the basic roles and responsibilities within the core project team for the performance of the project’s work activities (client sponsor, Engagement Partner, EM, team leads, and subject matter resources)?
  • What relationship exists with any third parties (e.g., another vendor)?

After establishing the governance structure, communications planning considers what type of information needs to be exchanged between the parties, and how the information will be structured, formatted, etc. Designing an effective communications plan depends on many factors. For example, a highly experienced team might need less formal intra-team communications than an inexperienced team. A large project may need to develop processes for consolidating information (e.g., a reporting hierarchy by work stream or geographic location).

A communication plan must provide a structure and schedule regarding the objectives, development, and distribution of information sent to the different audiences involved. The objectives of the communication plan are to:

  • Verify that project management processes and tool(s) are communicated and utilized.]
  • Improve communications between project managers, departmental heads and executives through adequate awareness and training and provide accurate and timely reports such as program status reports, management reports and issue escalation and resolution.
  • Facilitate the use of standard project management techniques, methodologies, and tools by the project managers in the management of the day-to-day project activities.
  • Establish structured, periodic dialog with key stakeholders regarding the performance of project.

To achieve the communications objectives, follow this four step approach:

  1. Target the audience to determine the identities, responsibilities and decision rights of key stakeholders.
  2. Define communication topics for creating awareness among stakeholders.
  3. Implement tools and techniques that will publicize PMO processes and tools to project teams.
  4. Develop a communications calendar that will permit structured, regular dialog with key stakeholders regarding the performance of project

The following table describes typical target audiences for the communication plan, along with their responsibilities.

Internal Stakeholders

Audience Position Description Responsibilities
Sponsor Internal The Sponsor leads the group within client organization. Hold ultimate responsibility for all communications within client organization
Business Lead Internal The Business Lead supports the projects within the client organization. Support and drive the initiative within client area of responsibility (e.g., Consumer Finance, Investment Bank)
Department Head Internal The Department Head heads the various departments within the client organization. Support and drive the initiative within Departments
Project Manager Internal The Project Manager manages a project or operational activities within client company. Adopt newly introduced project management practices in most effective manner within project teams

External Stakeholders

Audience Description Responsibilities
Board of Directors The Board of Directors is oversees the strategic posture of the organization. Overall strategic planning and decisions of organization

Define Communication Topics

As you define topics about which to communicate to your stakeholders, consider the following:

1. Project Planning

Scope Definition (Project Charter)
Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) Development
Project Scheduling
Project Estimation
Communications Planning
Stakeholder Identification
Resource Management

2. Project Execution

Status Reporting
Issue Management
Change Management
Risk Management
Quality Management

Implement Tools and Techniques

Consider the variety of tools and techniques that can be used to communicate effectively.

Tools & techniques Description
Presentations Face-to-face sessions coordinated and presented by specialized project personnel.
Training sessions Formal training sessions conducted on relevant project areas.
Discussions Focus group discussions among small groups of staff members conducted by the project team members.
E-Mail or voice mail Concise messages provided to communicate project related reminders, information or concerns.
Newsletter A periodic newsletter can be distributed on a regular basis to address a wide range of project issues, practices, and topics for stakeholders.
Company website Utilize the client’s company intranet site to disseminate project awareness information, best practices and other documents, as well as provide up-to-date status on programs. This is an optimum location to post information of an immediate nature.
Tutorials/Webcasts On-line courses in which the instructor Webcasts a pre-recorded or live lecture.

Develop communications plan and calendar

A good communication plan generally includes the following elements:

  • Communication objectives
  • Target audiences
  • Key content for the communications
  • Communication method and frequency
  • Complete the plan and each of its components to assist the project team in confirming all avenues of communication are addressed appropriately.
  • Utilize the stakeholder register and project charter to facilitate population of the plan. Populate the calendar, as needed, with scheduled events or meetings to help the team and client track key dates.

Develop a communications calendar that will be maintained by the project manager, which includes the methods (media) that will be used to deliver these communications, the frequency of communications, the targeted audience and the person with responsibility for creating and delivering the communications. The communications calendar is a “living” document that will be revised according to the needs of the project.
